messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Schur Complement
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to implement Mixture of Experts (ME) model, where the individual experts are Gaussian Process (GP) regression models.  For this I need to compute compute conditional distributions of multivariate normal multiple times or in linear algebra terms evaluate Schur complement of blocks in covariance matrix multiple times.  I wonder if there is a faster procedure than just brute-force approach (code below)?

Any suggestions are very appreciated.

Linas

model {
    // determine mu, Sigma for GP
    matrix [N, N] Sigma;
    vector [N] mu;
...
    for (n in 1 : N) {
        row_vector [N - 1] Sigma12;
        row_vector [N - 1] Sigma21;
        row_vector [N - 1] Sigma12_inv_Sigma22;
        matrix [N - 1, N - 1] Sigma22;
        vector [N - 1] mu2;
        vector [N - 1] a;

         // conditional distribution of y[n], given parameter mu, Sigma, and y[-n] (all data but y[n])
        // mu1 = mu [n]
        mu1 <- mu [n];
        // mu2 = mu [-n]
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1)) mu2 [i] <- mu [i];
        for (i in (n + 1) : N) mu2 [i - 1] <- mu [i];
        // a = y [-n]
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1)) a [i] <- y [i];
        for (i in (n + 1) : N) a [i - 1] <- y [i];
        // Sigma11 = Sigma [n,n]
        Sigma11 <- Sigma [n, n];
        // Sigma12 = Sigma [n, -n]
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1)) Sigma12 [i] <- Sigma [n, i];
        for (i in (n + 1) : N) Sigma12 [i - 1] <- Sigma [n, i];
        // Sigma21 = Sigma12'
        for (i in 1 : (N - 1)) Sigma21 [i] <- Sigma12 [i];
        // Sigma22 = Sigma [-n, -n]
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1))
            for (j in 1 : (n - 1))
                Sigma22 [i, j] <- Sigma [i, j];
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1))
            for (j in (n + 1) : N)
                Sigma22 [i, j - 1] <- Sigma [i, j];
        for (i in (n + 1) : N)
            for (j in 1 : (n - 1))
                Sigma22 [i - 1, j] <- Sigma [i, j];
        for (i in (n + 1) : N)
            for (j in (n + 1) : N)
                Sigma22 [i - 1, j - 1] <- Sigma [i, j];
        Sigma12_inv_Sigma22 <- Sigma12 / Sigma22;
        mu_star <- mu1 + Sigma12_inv_Sigma22 * (a - mu2);
        Sigma_star <- Sigma11 - Sigma12_inv_Sigma22 * Sigma21;
...
    }
}

messages.subject: Re: Schur Complement
parts:
It is no faster, but it would entail much less code to utilize the block() function described in section 30.5 of the manual.

Ben
